name: DIRECT V12262 M31C A
description: The primary star of DIRECT V12262 M31C, an eclipsing pair of hot stars in the Andromeda Galaxy, 21.7 solar masses and 9.2 solar radii; the two eclipse each other every 2.048644 days.

radius.source: Primary radius 9.2 +/- 0.2 solar radii, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

mass.source: Primary mass 21.7 +/- 1.7 solar masses, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

temperature.source: Primary Teff 33600 +/- 600 K, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 3

gravity.source: Primary log g 3.85 +/- 0.02 (cgs), Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

radialVelocity.source: Systemic velocity gamma -164 +/- 5 km/s of the pair, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2

distance.source: Placed in M31 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 769,731 pc (src/objects/m31/source/recipe.json: centre 776,247 pc from the Local Volume Database v1.1.1 (Pace 2025), inclination 74 deg, line of nodes 37.7 deg). The pair's own measured distance: Distance 724 +/- 37 kpc, (m-M)0 = 24.30 +/- 0.11 mag, from the pair's own radii, temperatures and brightness, Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 3; it is told in the text, and the star is drawn in the galaxy

text.card: The primary star of an eclipsing pair in the Andromeda Galaxy, one orbit every 2.048644 days.
text.introduction: It has 21.7 solar masses and 9.2 solar radii; its partner has 15.4 and 5.6. The pair gave a direct distance to the galaxy: 724 kiloparsecs.
text.locator: Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70, Table 2: M, R, P and the distance

notes: Masses, radii, temperatures, the orbit and the distance are all from Vilardell et al. (2010), A&A 509, A70.
